data.reason: This settles D1.f2: I adopt block_k 3 → 2 over the votes of B and C (A ○, B ×, C ×). The customer gain is now measured in two periods under different demand. In period 1 on-time rose by +9.2 on 5/5 seeds. Now on-time rises from 216.6 to 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds), late falls from 11.4 to 4.2, p95_wait_s falls from 138 to 110 and blocked s falls from 1824 to 936. The lowest on-time rate rises from 0.93 to 0.97 and unfinished stays at 0.0. These are real service gains: blocked time halves and the contract is unchanged, so 'on time' is not being redefined. This is what the KPI (K1) asks for. Customers have no vote and have already borne the known cost of about 7 extra late deliveries per period once. In D1 I accepted that cost on purpose, so that the vote question could be decided explicitly. Repeating it would make the company vote a standing veto over customer service. C's loss has fallen from about a third of its utility in period 1 to about 14% now (65.8 → 56.3), and B's is small (68.5 → 65.5). This is a real cost and I weigh it seriously, but it is smaller than the customer gain on the KPI's main goal. The main reservation is road violations rising from 19.0 to 28.0. I do not know their safety meaning. I accept this for one period and will reconsider reverting if it persists or grows. This is not a permanent licence to override votes: the override is limited to a change with consistent multi-period customer gains and no contract change. Option 2 (hold_limit 60s → 50s) is not offered here. Its gain of +0.4 on 2/5 seeds would not justify anything in any case.
assumptions: The measured gains under identical seeds carry over to the next period's actual demand.
The rise in road violations from 19.0 to 28.0 is about parking and eviction rules, not collisions or dangers to other road users.
B and C will not change their robot policies in ways that erase the gain within one period.
The constitution and process permit an operator decision to adopt a rule change whose company vote failed.
unknowns: What kinds of road violations increase, and whether any affect safety.
Why C loses so much under block_k 2, and whether a targeted rule could reduce its loss.
How B and C will adapt after the override, and how it affects their future cooperation and votes.
